summary: GAC's first small car for Australia undercuts the BYD Dolphin Premium and MG 4 Essence 64 while offering a similar-size battery, more power and far more rear legroom than either, and Australian reviewers consistently rate its ride comfort and cabin packaging above its price. The disagreement is over the software and the ownership case: CarExpert and EV Central found the touchscreen-only controls buggy and the driver-assist warnings intrusive, while CarsGuide and Chasing Cars were more forgiving and focused on the value. Everyone flags the same unknowns: a brand with no Australian resale history, roughly 30 dealers and no capped-price servicing, though a five-star ANCAP rating published in October 2026 has settled the safety question.
pros: 60kWh usable (62kWh gross) LFP pack and 430km WLTP range beat the BYD Dolphin Premium's 427km, and the $31,990 Premium lists $5000 below that BYD
150kW/210Nm and a 7.3-second 0-100km/h make it quicker than every rival under $40,000, including the MG 4 Essence 64
2750mm wheelbase and 905mm of rear legroom give it back-seat space a Toyota Corolla hatch cannot match, despite being 105mm shorter
Eight-year/unlimited-kilometre warranty is unconditional and two years longer than BYD's six or MG's seven
11kW AC charging as standard, against 7kW on the BYD Dolphin
cons: Five-star ANCAP (October 2026) came with weak scores for touchscreen-reliant controls, and the fitted eCall system will not be active until GAC's promised October 2027 switch-on
Climate and audio are buried in the 14.6-inch touchscreen with almost no physical controls, and reviewers report menu lag and outright bugs
87kW DC peak is slow for a 60kWh pack: about 40 minutes for 10-80 per cent, where an MG 4 64 manages a similar job faster
No capped-price servicing programme; GAC quotes $199-$640 a visit at dealer discretion and about $1607 over five years
Roughly 30 dealers nationally and no Australian resale track record, so residual values and parts supply are unproven
